description: Solo AI & systems engineering team building IGNIS-SI, an autonomous Super Intelligence dashboard that summarizes, ranks, and synthesizes NASA Physical Science Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion datasets to deliver actionable fire safety insights for spacecraft and lunar habitats.
summary: IGNIS-SI is a Super Intelligence (SI)-powered fire safety discovery dashboard that summarizes, ranks, and synthesizes NASA Physical Science Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion investigations. By matching spacecraft and lunar habitat atmospheric profiles (such as 30% O2 at 10.2 psi) against ISS experimental datasets across CIR and MSG hardware, it delivers verifiable flammability, aerosol detection, and suppression insights for Artemis, Mars transit, and terrestrial fire safety.
details: IGNIS-SI addresses the critical challenge of navigating decades of fragmented microgravity combustion data inside NASA's Physical Science Informatics (PSI) repository. Using a multi-stage Super Intelligence pipeline—combining domain-specific Named Entity Recognition (NER), hybrid late-interaction retrieval, and Bayesian contradiction mining—the system structures experimental variables including fuel geometry, oxygen concentration (21% to 85% O2), ambient pressure (down to 4.3 psi), airflow velocity, and sensor telemetry across Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) and Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) hardware. Engineers and researchers can input target crewed habitat parameters (such as lunar base 30% O2 / 10.2 psi environments) to rank relevant ISS investigations, compare suppression limits, bridge partial-gravity knowledge gaps via ACME E-FIELD Flames ahead of LUCI and FM2 missions, and extract dual-use terrestrial fire-safety spin-offs.
